title: How can two equal sticks and a thread make a right angle?
description: There is no paper to fold, only two sticks of equal length and a thread. The video crosses the sticks at their middles, runs the thread round the four ends, and uses the method of the crossing strips to see that every thread corner is a right angle.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal sticks crossed at their midpoints make a rectangle with the thread, so every thread corner is an exact right angle. Watch for students who cross the sticks anywhere and expect right angles.

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 4)
video_script.why: The child uses equal diagonals that cut each other in half to get an exact right angle without paper.
video_script.substitution: Cross two equal sticks at their middles, pass the thread round the four ends, and use the corners of the rectangle they make.
video_script.anchor: two sticks of equal length crossed at their middles at O, with a thread running round the four ends
video_script.payoff_line: Cross the two sticks at their middles, and every thread corner is exactly ninety degrees

final_answer.spoken: cross the two sticks at their middles, and every thread corner is exactly ninety degrees

maths_rules: the two sticks have equal length and cross so that O is the midpoint of both, so OA = OB = OC = OD
the sticks are the diagonals AC and BD; the thread through the four ends makes quadrilateral ABCD
for any crossing angle x, base angles of triangle AOB are 90 - x/2 and base angles of triangle AOD are x/2
each corner of ABCD is (90 - x/2) + x/2 = 90 degrees
opposite triangles match by SAS, so opposite sides are equal and ABCD is a rectangle
video_script.design: One idea: equal sticks crossed at their middles give a rectangle with the thread. The sticks and the thread stay on the board from the ground beat to the check.
